tone_statements.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613 (Studies in Language Change 8). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, The Australian National University. xv+298 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Tone mergers can obscure this pattern. Iu Mien of Chiang Rai shows breathiness only in category B2, but C2 and D2 have merged into a 11 tone (Downer 1961, Purnell, forthcoming) which obscures the original distribution of phonation types. Similarly, Biao Min shows breathiness only in category A2, but B2, C2, and D2 have merged into a 42ʔ tone (Solnit 1985:182). Since A2 is breathy, it is likely that both B2 and C2 were breathy originally, and the merged tone terminated by a glottal stop reflects the detritus of final stop consonants.
tone_statements.locator: p. 194, chapter 3, section 3.3.1 'Distribution of low-pitch tones in modern languages', footnote 59

tone_statements.quote: 2.4 声調 (Tone) CKM には声調の音韻的単位である調類は、7つある。そのうちの6つが祖語の4つの声調の発展であり、残りの1つは祖語の声調と直接にはつながらないものである。[…] これが、CKM では他のミエン語と同様、*A, *B, *C の各声調は音節頭子音の有声・無声を条件として2つに分岐したが、*D 声調は音節末子音を失って、他の声調に合流した。[…] 表3．CKM の声調 […] 調類 1 2 3 4 5 6 (1/3) (2/4) 7 ／ 調値 433 45 13 42 44 22 - - 21 […] 声調交替現象は、音声的なものが観察される。それは、第3声調は他の声調の前で中平調 [33] で発音されるというものである。
tone_statements.translation: 2.4 Tone. CKM has seven tonemes (tone categories), the phonological units of tone. Six of them are developments of the four tones of the proto-language; the remaining one is not directly connected to the proto-language tones. [...] In CKM, as in the other Mienic languages, each of the tones *A, *B, *C split into two conditioned by the voicing of the syllable-initial consonant, whereas tone *D lost the syllable-final consonants and merged with the other tones. [...] Table 3. The tones of CKM [...] tone category 1 2 3 4 5 6 (1/3) (2/4) 7 / tone value 433 45 13 42 44 22 - - 21 [...] A tone alternation of a phonetic kind is observed: tone 3 is pronounced as a mid level tone [33] before another tone.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 76-77, section 2.4 声調 (Tone) and 表3 (CKM の声調)

sources.note: First-hand fieldwork (2009). Sec. 2.4 Tone: CKM has 7 tonemes; six continue the four proto-tones (*A, *B, *C each split in two by onset voicing; *D lost its final stops and merged into tones 1/3 after voiceless onsets and 2/4 after voiced onsets), the seventh (tone 7) is not traceable to a proto-tone and occurs in some Chinese loans, kinship terms and pronouns. Table 3 tone values: 1 = 433, 2 = 45, 3 = 13, 4 = 42, 5 = 44, 6 = 22, 7 = 21. Phonetic detail: tone 1 starts fairly high, falls slightly then level; tone 2 highest, rising with stiff voice; tone 3 with marked breathy voice at onset; to…
